name: Gus Kemper
summary: A tall, quiet custodian on the day crew who cleans Vira's data halls and goes home to raise his one-year-old daughter, Valeria, mostly by himself. He is slow to talk and quick to notice, does the job exactly right, and is held together by his mother, his crew and a lot of gas-station coffee.

backstory.childhood: Born November 19, 1994, and raised in Kingman, Arizona, in a rented single-wide behind a muffler shop off Andy Devine Avenue. His mother, Darlene, worked the deli counter at a grocery store and later cleaned rooms at a motel on Route 66. He was the kid who sat in the back of the classroom drawing trains in the margins. He played two seasons of JV basketball because he was tall, not because he was good, and quit when he realized the coach only liked him for the rebounds. The best summer of his childhood was the one he spent at his uncle's place outside Bullhead City, fixing a dirt bike that never ran right.
backstory.family_of_origin: His father, Ray Kemper, drove truck and was gone more than he was home; he left for good when Gus was nine and now lives in Oklahoma with a second family. They text on birthdays, sometimes. His mother Darlene raised him and his younger sister, Shayla, who is now a dental assistant in Lake Havasu City with two boys. Darlene remarried in 2016 to a retired railroad man named Lloyd and moved with him to Ironwood, which is the whole reason Gus ended up there. Lloyd died in 2023. Darlene, 58, lives alone four blocks from Gus and keeps Valeria every weekday morning from 5 AM until Gus gets home.
backstory.education: Kingman High School, graduated 2013 with a 2.4 and a woodshop award he still keeps in a drawer. He did one semester at Mohave Community College in general studies and stopped going when his car died and the bus schedule didn't work. He has an OSHA 10 card and a forklift certification from the warehouse years, and he's taken every safety module Vira has put in front of him, including the electrostatic discharge one twice because he failed the quiz the first time by clicking too fast.
backstory.before_vira: After high school he worked as a porter at a casino in Laughlin for four years: vacuuming the floor at 3 AM, emptying ashtrays, cleaning up after people who'd had a very bad night. Then three years at a distribution warehouse in North Las Vegas loading trailers, where he learned to work fast and say nothing. In 2020 the warehouse cut his shift and he moved into his mother and Lloyd's spare room in Ironwood 'for a couple months' that turned into a year and a half. He did odd jobs: two summers stacking pallets at one of the warehouses south of the tracks, a stretch washing dishes at the diner on Main Street, and part-time nights at the laundromat folding drop-off loads.
backstory.how_they_came_to_vira: In the summer of 2024, Mateo Trujillo posted in a Facebook group that the Vira custodial crew was hiring. Gus applied that night on his phone. Rosa Mahoney interviewed him in a conference room in the operations building and asked him one real question, which was what he'd do if he spilled a full bucket in a hall. He said he'd stop, put out the cones, call it in and not try to hide it. She hired him in August 2024. Mateo trained him for his first two weeks, mostly by showing him what not to touch.
turning_points: Moving to Ironwood in 2020 with everything he owned in the back of a borrowed pickup, and admitting to himself that he was a grown man living in his mother's spare room.
Meeting Brianna at the saloon in Ironwood in late 2023; she was passing through on her way back from a job in Barstow and stayed a year.
Valeria being born in September 2025 at a hospital in Halcyon, at 2:40 in the morning, after a nineteen-hour labor. He drove home with the car seat checked four times.
Brianna leaving in January 2026 for Phoenix, saying she wasn't built for this. Gus got primary custody without a fight. She video-calls most Sundays and sends money when she can.
Getting through his first full summer as a single father on an early shift, which he counts as the hardest thing he's done and the thing he's proudest of.

household_notes.note: Thirteen months old, walking since August, wobbling between the couch and the coffee table like a drunk sailor. She has his black hair and a cowlick that won't lie down. She says 'Da,' 'ba' for bottle, 'uh-oh' for everything that hits the floor, and something that sounds like 'Gwah' for her grandmother. She's a bad sleeper and wakes at 3 AM about twice a week, which means Gus is often running on four hours. Her bedtime routine is bath, one book about a tugboat, the white-noise machine set to rain, and him sitting on the floor next to the crib until she's out. The duplex at 100 Whistle Stop Lane is mostly baby gates, a playpen and a basket of clean laundry he never gets around to folding.

traits: Quiet; will let a silence go on longer than most people can stand
Observant, notices a scuff mark or a mood before anyone else does
Patient with kids, machines and old people; short with people who make messes on purpose
Stubborn about doing things right even when nobody's checking
Self-deprecating, quick to assume he's the one who screwed up
Loyal past the point of good sense
values: Show up on time, every time
Leave a place cleaner than you found it
Don't make your problems somebody else's problems
Take care of your own; Valeria first, then his mom, then his crew
fears: That Valeria will grow up and decide he wasn't enough
Getting sick or hurt and having nobody to take her
Losing the job over something stupid, like knocking a cable loose in a hall
Becoming his father: a man who is always somewhere else
personality.humor: Dry and late. He'll say nothing for five minutes and then drop one flat line that makes Mateo spit out his coffee. He likes dumb puns and pretends he doesn't. He's funniest about himself: 'I'm not tired. I've just been awake since 2023.'
personality.temper: Slow to anger and quiet when he gets there. He goes very still, says 'Okay' in a low voice and walks away. The few times he has really lost it, it was over somebody being rough with a kid or a woman, and both times he regretted the shouting more than the reason.
quirks: Folds the corner of every trash bag liner into a neat triangle before setting it
Keeps a pacifier clipped to his badge lanyard by accident about once a week
Hums the theme from the tugboat cartoon without knowing he's doing it
Counts mop strokes in his head in sets of eight
Always parks in the same row of the staff lot, three spaces from the light pole, so he can find his car half-asleep

voice.how_they_talk: Low, slow and short. He answers questions with as few words as will do the job and rarely asks one back unless he cares. Sentences trail off when he's tired. He swears mildly and only around adults: 'dang,' 'shoot,' and a real one when he drops something heavy. When he's explaining how to do something right he suddenly gets full sentences and a little bit of authority.
voice.vocabulary: Plain working words. Casino and warehouse leftovers: 'eighty-six it,' 'on the clock,' 'that's a two-man lift.' Baby talk has started creeping into his adult speech: he's said 'uh-oh' out loud when dropping a mop head and called a spill a 'mess-mess.' He says 'yes ma'am' to every woman over forty.
phrases: That's a wet floor, man, that's literally what the sign means.
I'm not tired. I've just been awake since 2023.
She's good. She's a terror, but she's good.
voice.with_strangers: Polite and almost invisible. Nods, steps aside, says 'morning' and keeps working. New engineers sometimes don't notice he's in the aisle until he says 'behind you.' If a stranger asks him a question he answers it exactly and doesn't add anything.
voice.with_friends: Loosens up. Teases Mateo about his truck, lets Lena mother him, will show anybody who asks forty videos of Valeria walking. With Mateo he can talk for twenty minutes straight about nothing, mostly about trucks, the heat and whatever stupid thing Pete Yazzie said that morning.

daily_life.workday: Alarm at 4:15. Bottle and diaper for Valeria in the dark, carries her sleeping in the car seat four blocks to his mother's house by 4:55, and is on the highway by 5:05 with a gas-station coffee from the highway strip in Ironwood. Clocks in at 5:55. The crew meets at the custodial closet behind the operations building, gets assignments off Rosa Mahoney's whiteboard notes from the night before, and splits up by block. Gus usually works the B and C halls: changing the tacky mats at the hall entrances, running the HEPA vacuums down the aisles, damp-mopping only where it's allowed, wiping door hardware and badge readers, emptying the break-area trash and checking the restroom supplies. Lunch at 10:30 in the cafeteria or in his car with the AC running and his eyes closed for fifteen minutes. Clocks out at 2:30, which is usually right when Rosa Mahoney is coming in, so they get two minutes of handoff in the hallway. Home by 3:20, picks up Valeria, and the second shift starts.
daily_life.after_work: Takes Valeria from his mom's, usually stays for a glass of iced tea while Darlene tells him what Valeria ate and how many times she fell down. Home by 4. Floor time with the baby, dinner for both of them (she eats a lot of what he eats, mashed), a walk around the block once it drops under a hundred, bath, tugboat book, bed. He's usually asleep himself by 9, sometimes on the couch with the TV still on.
daily_life.days_off: Saturdays are errands: the laundromat if his washer is acting up again, the grocery run, the hardware store on Main Street for whatever broke that week. Valeria rides on his shoulders. Sundays his mother makes a pot roast and Brianna video-calls around 4, and Gus holds the phone up so Valeria can see her mom, then goes in the other room while they talk.
hobbies: Model railroading, in theory; there's an HO-scale layout half-built on a door slab in his closet that hasn't been touched since Valeria was born
Watching train-cam livestreams on his phone at night
Fixing small things for his mom's neighbors: a screen door, a ceiling fan
Taking about two hundred photos of Valeria a week
daily_life.food: Whatever is fast. Gas-station breakfast burritos, frozen pizzas, the cafeteria's lunch plate when he can afford it. He loves his mother's pot roast and the green chile stew Kofi makes in the cafeteria on Tuesdays. He has started actually cooking, slowly, because Valeria needs vegetables and he figured he should eat them too: rice, beans, steamed carrots, scrambled eggs. He drinks too much coffee and too little water.
daily_life.music: Old country his mother played in the car: Alan Jackson, George Strait, Randy Travis. Some early 2000s rock from high school, Linkin Park and Three Doors Down, that he won't defend. In the car before dawn he mostly listens to nothing at all, just the road.
hangouts: The laundromat in Ironwood, Saturday mornings
The highway strip gas station in Ironwood at 5 AM
The cafeteria at Vira, the corner table by the window
The hardware store on Main Street in Ironwood

work.what_they_actually_do: Keeps the data halls clean enough for the machines, which is a different kind of clean than people think. Dust is the enemy: it clogs filters and gets into equipment, so most of the job is vacuuming with HEPA machines, changing out the sticky mats at the hall doors so people don't track desert in, wiping down surfaces with the approved antistatic stuff, and never, ever using a wet mop near a rack. He also does trash, restrooms and break areas in the halls, logs any damage he sees (a cracked floor tile, a stuck door, a leak) in the facilities ticket system, and gets out of the way when the technicians are working. He has to badge into every hall, follow the escort rules in the restricted areas and keep his cart out of the aisles during maintenance.
work.how_good_they_are: Very good. He's thorough to the point that Rosa Mahoney uses his hall as the example when training new people. He's caught two small coolant drips and a door that wasn't latching before anyone on the engineering side did, and filed the tickets cleanly. His one weakness is speed: he won't cut a corner, so on heavy days he runs right up to the end of his shift.
work.how_they_feel_about_the_job: Grateful, mostly. It's the best-paying job he's ever had, it has health insurance that covered Valeria's birth, and the work is quiet. He likes the halls: cold, humming, nobody bothering him. He doesn't love the early shift now that he has a baby, and he has thought about asking for swing, but Rosa Mahoney's on swing and the day crew is his crew.
work.opinion_of_vira: A big humming box full of computers that pays well and doesn't ask much. He doesn't really know what it does, and he figures it's not his business: 'Internet stuff. Cloud.' He thinks the managers in the operations building are fine, mostly invisible. He respects the engineers who say thank you and has a short private list of the ones who don't.
work.ambition: Small and specific. He'd like to make lead custodian someday, maybe when Rosa Mahoney retires. He'd like to save enough to buy a house in Ironwood with a yard so Valeria can have a swing set. He's thought, vaguely, about going back to school for HVAC, because he's seen what the cooling guys make, but not until Valeria's in school.

relationships.name: Rosa Mahoney
relationships.history: Rosa Mahoney hired him in August 2024 after one real interview question about a spilled bucket. Because she works 2:30 to 11 PM and he works 6 to 2:30, most of their relationship happens through her whiteboard notes in the custodial closet and two minutes of handoff in the hallway at 2:30. When Valeria was born she rearranged the day crew's assignments so he could take a full week of leave without anybody covering his halls badly, and she left a card and a gift card for diapers on his locker.
relationships.how_they_feel: Respects her enormously and is a little afraid of disappointing her. He thinks she's the fairest boss he's ever had. He'd like her job someday and feels guilty for wanting it.

relationships.name: Mateo Trujillo
relationships.history: Mateo posted the job in a Facebook group, then trained Gus for his first two weeks in 2024. They clicked over trucks and silence: Mateo talks, Gus listens, and that works. The night in January 2026 when Brianna left, Gus texted only one person, and Mateo drove forty-five minutes from Saltbrush with a bag of groceries, a case of diapers and a twelve-pack, and sat on the floor with him until midnight. Neither of them has mentioned it since, which is how Gus knows it mattered.
relationships.how_they_feel: Best friend, though he'd never use those words out loud. If something happened to Gus, Mateo is the person he'd want to call his mom. He gives Mateo endless grief about the noise his truck makes.

relationships.name: Lena Dorsey
relationships.history: Lena is the oldest-feeling person on the crew, not by age but by manner. They also live in Ironwood, alone, and took one look at Gus in his first month back after Valeria was born and decided he needed help. They taught him to swaddle in the custodial closet using a clean shop towel and a roll of paper towels as the baby. Lena watches Valeria a couple of Saturday mornings a month so Gus can sleep in or get the oil changed, and they always send her home with something knitted.
relationships.how_they_feel: Deep gratitude and a little awe. Lena is the closest thing he has to a second parent at work. He worries he takes more than he gives and has started fixing things at Lena's place on Signal Road to even it out.

relationships.name: Pete Yazzie
relationships.history: Pete commutes all the way in from Halcyon, which Gus thinks is insane. They share the C-block rotation two days a week. Pete talks constantly about Halcyon's sports teams and city traffic and new restaurants, and Gus has learned to say 'huh' in the right places. Pete bought Valeria a tiny jersey for one of the Halcyon teams, which Gus put on her once for a photo for him.
relationships.how_they_feel: Likes him fine. Pete's a good worker and a nice guy who wears Gus out. They are work friends, not after-work friends.

relationships.name: Dana Dominguez
relationships.history: Dana is the crew's family man with a teenage son and a grown daughter, and his wife is one of the facilities engineers. When Gus mentioned in the break area that Valeria was starting solids, Dana showed up the next Monday with his son Elijah's old high chair in the back of his car, thirteen years old and still solid. Beyond that they mostly talk about whose hall has the worst sticky-mat traffic.
relationships.how_they_feel: Friendly, grateful about the high chair, not close. He thinks of Dana as a guy who's already been through what he's going through and is proof you come out the other side.

relationships.name: Shane Nunez
relationships.history: Shane is 59 and has been on the crew longest after Mateo. In the spring of 2025, when Gus's SUV needed a new water pump, Shane drove him to and from Vira from Ironwood for nine days. Shane listens to talk radio at a volume that made Gus's ears ring, and lectures about pensions and his bad knees, and never once took gas money.
relationships.how_they_feel: Fond of him the way you are of a grumpy uncle. Gus doesn't agree with half of what's on Shane's radio but owes him, and Shane knows a lot about how the halls used to be.

relationships.name: Mei Pruitt
relationships.history: They met in April 2026 at the laundromat in Ironwood, both there on a Saturday morning with a baby on the hip, his Valeria and her Sadie, who are a few months apart. Mei recognized his Vira badge on the dashboard. They've since become laundromat friends who text each other about teething gels, sleep regressions and which size of diapers runs small. Mei has two grown sons too, so she knows things, and she's given him a garbage bag of Sadie's outgrown clothes twice.
relationships.how_they_feel: Likes her a lot and is a little intimidated: she works in an office at Vira doing math he doesn't understand. It's the only friendship he has where they're both single parents and nobody has to explain the tired.

relationships.name: Kofi Irving
relationships.history: Kofi runs the cafeteria kitchen. In October 2025, Gus's first week back after Valeria was born, he came through the lunch line gray-faced, and Kofi asked him what was wrong. When Gus said he had a newborn at home and no one cooking, Kofi started handing him a deli container of rice and stew or soft beans at the end of service 'because it's going in the trash anyway.' It still happens about once a week. They don't talk much beyond that.
relationships.how_they_feel: Embarrassed by the kindness and grateful for it. He thinks Kofi is the best cook he's ever met and that the green chile stew alone is worth the commute.

wants: A house with a yard in Ironwood before Valeria starts school
For Valeria to have a real relationship with her mom, even long-distance
To finish the train layout someday with Valeria old enough to run the switches
To be good enough at the job that nobody ever thinks of letting him go
worries: His mother is 58, has high blood pressure and is doing too much; if she gets sick, the whole morning plan falls apart
Money, always; the duplex rent went up $75 in June
That he's missing things in Valeria's life because she's asleep when he leaves
That Brianna will come back someday and want custody
His own back, which has started to ache after the vacuum shifts
secrets: He still has Brianna's hoodie in his closet and hasn't decided whether that means anything.
He cried in the restroom in Hall C3 the week after she left, once, for about two minutes, and then mopped the floor.
He applied for a swing-shift opening in May 2026 and withdrew the application the same day without telling Mateo.
inner_life.regrets: Quitting community college over a dead car when he could have figured something out. And the year he spent in his mother's spare room feeling sorry for himself while Lloyd was getting sick; he wishes he'd spent more of it actually talking to Lloyd.

health_and_money.health: Generally healthy and strong from the work, but chronically short on sleep. A lower-back ache from the HEPA vacuum harness that he treats with ibuprofen and a heating pad. He's down about fifteen pounds since Valeria was born, mostly from skipping meals. He hasn't been to a doctor for himself since 2022 but takes Valeria to every checkup and has the vaccine schedule taped to the fridge.
health_and_money.money: Tight but not drowning. Vira's custodial pay is the best he's made. Rent on the duplex is $1,150. He pays his mother $100 a week for the childcare even though she tries to refuse it, and she puts it in an envelope she thinks he doesn't know about, for Valeria. He has about $1,900 in savings, a $3,000 balance on one credit card from the birth and the move, and four years left on a loan for the beige SUV, which has a cracked windshield from a highway rock that he keeps meaning to get fixed. Brianna sends $200 or $300 most months.

beliefs.faith: Raised loosely Baptist by his mother; hasn't been to church as an adult except for Lloyd's funeral. He doesn't say he doesn't believe. He prayed in the hospital the night Valeria was born, hard, and figures that counts for something. He might start taking her to the church in Saltbrush when she's older, for his mother's sake.
beliefs.politics: Doesn't follow it and mostly doesn't vote; he voted once, in 2020, and felt like it didn't change anything. Distrusts politicians of every kind on principle. His actual opinions are practical: he thinks childcare should cost less, rents are crazy, and the highway to Vira needs a passing lane. He keeps all of it to himself and leaves the break room when Shane and Pete start arguing.

knowledge.about_vira: Knows the halls physically better than most engineers: which doors stick, which aisles run coldest, which badge readers are slow, where the sticky mats get the worst traffic. He knows Vira opened in 2019 and has sixteen halls in four blocks. He knows the generator yard is loud and the cooling yard is louder. He doesn't know or care what the computers are doing; 'cloud stuff.'
knowledge.about_lyra: Has never heard the name. As far as he knows Vira runs on ordinary automation and building controls. He's noticed a couple of odd things over two years: hall lights coming up in an aisle a beat before he reached the motion sensor, a hall door in C2 that clicked unlocked before he'd tapped his badge. He mentioned the door to Mateo, who said the readers do that, and Gus filed a ticket and forgot about it.
knowledge.about_marcus: Knows Marcus by sight: a guy who rides a motorcycle in from Saltbrush and works in the halls. He's passed him in an aisle and nodded. Nothing more than that.
rumors_they_believe: That the company is going to add a second custodial shift overnight once the array expansion is done
That one of the generator yard guys got walked out last year for sleeping in a truck, though nobody will say who
That the cafeteria's green chile stew recipe came from Kofi's mother-in-law, which isn't true

memories.what: His first day at Vira. Mateo walked him through Hall B1 and said, 'Rule one: you don't touch anything with a blinking light. Rule two: everything has a blinking light.' Gus spent the first hour scared to vacuum near the racks. By the end of the week Mateo was letting him run his own aisle.

Nine days of rides from Shane while the SUV was in the shop. Talk radio at full volume at 5 AM, Shane's opinion on everything, and on the last morning Shane handed him a thermos of coffee and said, 'You're a good kid, you just need to talk more.' Gus said 'Okay' and Shane laughed for a mile.

Rosa Mahoney stayed past the end of her shift, nearly midnight, so she could catch him by text and tell him not to come in for a week and that she'd already covered his halls. The text ended, 'Go hold your baby.' He still has it.

His first week back after Valeria was born. He hadn't eaten all day and came through the lunch line looking, as Kofi later told him, 'like a ghost who forgot where he lives.' Kofi asked what was going on and then handed him a deli container of rice and red stew at the end of service, and another the next day. Mateo was behind him in line and pretended not to notice.

Lena taught him to swaddle in the custodial closet using a shop towel and a roll of paper towels. Dana walked in in the middle of it, watched for a second and said, 'Tighter at the shoulders,' and walked out again.

The night Brianna left. He texted Mateo two words, 'she left,' and Mateo showed up from Saltbrush forty-five minutes later with groceries, diapers and beer. They sat on the floor with their backs against the couch and watched a monster truck rally on TV with the sound off while Valeria slept.

Meeting Mei at the laundromat in Ironwood: both of them trying to fold sheets one-handed with a baby on the other arm. She said, 'You work at Vira, right?' and then, 'Here, give me that corner.' They folded each other's sheets, and the babies stared at each other the whole time.

Valeria's first real steps, in his mother's kitchen, on a Tuesday afternoon right after he got home from work. He'd missed so much because of the early shift that his mother made him sit on the floor and wait an hour so he'd be the one she walked to. He showed the video to the whole crew the next morning, and Pete Yazzie made him play it three times.

conversation_starters: Ask him how Valeria is sleeping and he'll actually answer, at length.
Mention trains and watch him come alive; he can tell you which freight lines run through Ironwood and when.
Ask what's the dirtiest hall at Vira and why.
Ask about the half-built train layout in his closet.
Ask him about Kingman, or the casino in Laughlin at 3 AM; he has stories he never tells unless asked.
Ask whether he's going for lead custodian someday and watch him get embarrassed.
